newsitem.title: USA: AMR CEO sees fuel prices pressuring costs.
newsitem.headline: AMR CEO sees fuel prices pressuring costs.

text.p: AMR Corp chief executive Robert Crandall said on Thursday he expects American Airlines to record "quite a decent" fourth quarter profit but pointed to continuing cost pressures caused by high jet fuel prices.
Crandall said at a business forum that he does not expect to see an easing of fuel prices, which have jumped in recent months.
He said U.S. inventories of jet fuel are "very very shallow" and that would bring costs pressures in the fourth quarter.
"I think fuel prices will likely be under pressure right through the fall," Crandall said.
"We'll have quite a decent profit (in the fourth quarter), but the rate of improvement year over year is likely to slow down," he said.
"Bookings are solid but not as strong as they've been earlier. On the other hand, average yields are holding up, so the fact of the matter is that we'll have an okay quarter," he said.
Crandall said he was confident the proposed American Airlines alliance with British Airways Plc would clear regulatory hurdles on both sides of the Atlantic.
"We've also got to get an open skies agreement done, but I think in due course both of those things will happen," he said.
AMR shares were up two points at 84-5/8 at 1330 EDT/1730 GMT.
